limitations: Retrospective, single-institution experience with practice variation even within the institution - for example no universal approach to diagnosing peritoneal disease, so not every patient had staging laparoscopy

The proportion with metastatic disease at diagnosis (34%) is low relative to national cohorts and major centres where up to 47% present metastatic; the population appears skewed toward patients undergoing curative-intent treatment with fewer systemic-only patients, possibly because chemotherapy was given at local hospitals
The cohort predates the current electronic medical record, so not all patients had complete data (such as CA19-9) or available imaging for review
Because CA19-9 availability varied, it was deliberately NOT used as a criterion for selecting the hypothetical benchmark cohort, even though CA19-9 trend is likely to inform real clinical decisions
The authors state that to the best of their knowledge no published study has compared resected patients with patients who survived to the same landmark time without surgery
critique: COMPARATOR: this paper IS the comparator, and that is its contribution - it supplies the control arm that Hamad, D'Ambra, Clements and every single-centre resection series lack. Its own weakness is the mirror image: it has no surgical arm, so it cannot exclude a real benefit from resection, only show that most of the reported benefit is explained by selection

THE BENCHMARK REST ON NINE PATIENTS. A median of 39 months with a 95% CI of 13 months to not-reached is an estimate from 9 people, 5 of whom had died. The paper is appropriately explicit that this is a 'hypothetical cohort', but a 9-patient benchmark is a fragile standard against which to judge surgical series of 30-250 patients, and the direction of its own imprecision is unknown

THE 12-MONTH LANDMARK IS ITSELF ARBITRARY AND BORROWED. It was chosen because two published series had a median 10 months from diagnosis to surgery. Series with a shorter interval (6-8 months in one cited study) face less immortal time bias, so a single 12-month landmark over-corrects for some comparisons and under-corrects for others; no sensitivity analysis across landmark times is presented

ONLY 80 OF 183 PATIENTS WITH LIVER METASTASIS HAD IMAGING AVAILABLE FOR REVIEW (44%), and resectability - the paper's only significant prognostic variable - could only be assigned in that subset. Whether imaging was retrievable is unlikely to be independent of where and how intensively a patient was treated

RESECTABILITY WAS ASSESSED BY THE AUTHORS RETROSPECTIVELY AND UNBLINDED TO OUTCOME, using criteria adapted from colorectal liver metastasis. The finding that liver resectability predicts survival (HR 0.51) is therefore partly a judgement made with knowledge of the clinical course, and resectability was itself strongly correlated with metastatic burden (P<0.001) - so it may be a proxy for disease volume rather than an independent factor

THE COHORT IS UNREPRESENTATIVE IN A DIRECTION THE AUTHORS ACKNOWLEDGE BUT UNDERSTATE: 34% presented with metastatic disease versus up to 47% nationally, and 29% received no chemotherapy at all with 11% of those going to hospice. A referral cohort at an academic centre that captures few systemic-only patients will overstate survival at every level, which if anything makes the benchmark MORE conservative - but it also means the 7-month baseline median is not a national figure

STAGING LAPAROSCOPY WAS NOT ROUTINE, so some patients classified as liver-only had undetected peritoneal disease; conversely patients with occult peritoneal disease are exactly who a surgical series would exclude at exploration, which biases the comparison against the non-surgical benchmark

CA 19-9 WAS DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED FROM THE SELECTION CRITERIA, and 64% of the benchmark cohort had RISING CA19-9. In practice no surgeon would operate on a patient with a rising marker, so the benchmark cohort is less favourably selected than a real surgical cohort on the single most used biological criterion - which cuts against the paper's argument that the groups are comparable

The paper does not report how many of the 241 patients received multi-agent versus single-agent chemotherapy by subgroup beyond 81% overall, nor duration of therapy, so the benchmark's 26- and 39-month survivals cannot be attributed to a specified systemic regimen

A pathway should take the methodological lesson (landmark analysis is mandatory, resected-only denominators are uninterpretable) as the durable finding, and treat the 39-month figure itself as a 9-patient estimate

36353987.bottom_line: This single-centre natural-history study is the control group the oligometastatic pancreatic surgery literature never had: patients with liver-only metastatic PDAC who received chemotherapy and survived 12 months had a median survival of 26 months, and the 4% who were also theoretically operable reached 39 months with NO surgery at all - matching or exceeding most published resection series and showing that conditional survival, not resection, explains their results, though the benchmark itself rests on only nine patients and there were no 5-year survivors.

Patients with investigator-determined progression who started subsequent therapy were censored in the independent analysis, contributing to the discrepancy between the two DFS results
There was no central pathology review and there may have been regional differences in standards for defining R0 versus R1 across the 21 countries
Comparisons with ESPAC-4 and other trials are not valid because of differences in patient selection and subsequent therapy
Because the primary endpoint was not met, all other comparisons are considered descriptive
critique: COMPARATOR: adjuvant gemcitabine monotherapy, chosen in 2013 and already obsolete before the trial reported - ESPAC-4 appeared in 2017 and PRODIGE-24 in 2018, both while APACT was in follow-up. The control arm did NOT receive modern adjuvant therapy, and the authors themselves note gemcitabine/capecitabine and mFOLFIRINOX had become category 1 preferred regimens after APACT started

NON-RECEIPT OF ALLOCATED TREATMENT: 3/432 (1%) and 11/434 (3%) were randomised but never treated, and 93% of each arm formed the per-protocol population - low and balanced. Delivery, however, was poor: only 66% and 71% completed six cycles, and 64% of combination patients needed a dose reduction

THIS IS A NEGATIVE TRIAL WHOSE POSITIVE SECONDARY ENDPOINT IS WIDELY QUOTED. The primary endpoint failed (HR 0.88, P=.18). Any pathway citing '41.8 vs 37.7 months, P=.0091' is citing a descriptive secondary analysis from a failed trial, and no multiplicity adjustment was applied to any of it

THREE SUCCESSIVE OVERALL SURVIVAL CUTOFFS WERE REPORTED (December 2018, April 2020, April 2021) and the P value improved from .045 to .0232 to .0091 across them, with no prespecified plan for repeated testing. Reporting the most favourable of three looks at the same secondary endpoint, in a trial whose primary endpoint failed, is the clearest example of unadjusted multiplicity in this depot

THE INDEPENDENT-VERSUS-INVESTIGATOR DFS DISCREPANCY IS THE MOST VALUABLE FINDING IN THE PAPER AND CUTS AGAINST EVERY OTHER ADJUVANT TRIAL. In the same gemcitabine arm, blinded central review gave 18.8 months and investigators gave 13.7 months. Every other adjuvant pancreatic trial (CONKO-001, ESPAC-4, PRODIGE-24) used unblinded investigator-assessed DFS as its primary endpoint and reported 12.8-13.4 months. APACT shows that this endpoint is systematically shorter when assessed by the unblinded treating physician, which means DFS differences in open-label adjuvant trials are partly a detection artefact - a point no pathway citing those trials' DFS results should ignore

THE CENSORING RULE IS ASYMMETRIC AND FAVOURS NEITHER ARM BUT DESTROYS THE PRIMARY ENDPOINT. Patients were censored in the independent review once they started subsequent therapy, so patients whom investigators judged to be progressing and treated accordingly simply left the analysis; 48-51% of patients were censored. An endpoint that censores half the cohort for acting on clinical judgement is not measuring disease-free survival

THE POPULATION IS THE MOST HIGHLY SELECTED IN THE ADJUVANT LITERATURE: CA 19-9 below 100 U/mL (80% were within normal limits and median CA19-9 was 13.6 U/mL), a clear screening scan, ECOG 0-1, and 76% R0. One thousand two hundred and twenty-six patients were screened to randomise 866. The 37.7-month gemcitabine-arm survival far exceeds CONKO-001's 22.8 months and reflects this selection, not improved therapy

NO CENTRAL PATHOLOGY REVIEW ACROSS 160 SITES IN 21 COUNTRIES, so R0/R1 - a stratification factor and the strongest prognostic variable in ESPAC-4 - was assigned to local standards that the authors concede varied regionally

PERMANENT NEUROPATHY IS THE UNPRICED COST: 15% grade 3 or higher peripheral neuropathy versus 0%, with 84% unresolved to grade 1 or better at the primary cutoff, in a trial that failed its primary endpoint and collected NO quality-of-life data. The regimen is recommended in the conclusion as an option for patients who cannot take mFOLFIRINOX without quantifying this trade-off

SUBSEQUENT THERAPY WAS ASYMMETRIC: 21% of gemcitabine patients received nab-paclitaxel-based therapy at relapse versus 8% of combination patients, so the control arm partly crossed over to the experimental drug, which if anything attenuates the observed difference

THE TRIAL WAS DESIGNED, MONITORED AND ANALYSED BY THE SPONSOR. limitations: Recruitment was challenging and the original target of 100 patients was not reached; some centres recruited fewer than two patients per year because of set-up difficulties and investigator reluctance to delay surgery
As a feasibility study with low numbers there are methodological limitations and the possibility of random confounding from baseline imbalance
Non-adherence to treatment and the nature of comparing a surgical intervention with neoadjuvant therapy introduce potential bias
The short minimum follow-up of 12 months and low event rate make the hazard ratios imprecise and make non-proportionality impossible to assess, so survival data should be interpreted with caution
The low R0 rates may reflect the strict <1 mm R0 definition as well as the borderline resectable population
The study was not powered to compare resection rates between individual treatment groups
critique: COMPARATOR: immediate surgery followed by adjuvant therapy at the clinician's discretion. THE CONTROL ARM DID NOT RECEIVE MODERN ADJUVANT THERAPY: of 43 patients who received adjuvant treatment across the whole trial, 41 (95%) got gemcitabine or gemcitabine plus capecitabine and only 2 (5%) got modified FOLFIRINOX, because combination adjuvant therapy only became available near the end of the trial. The 39% 1-year survival in the immediate surgery arm reflects surgery plus gemcitabine-era adjuvant therapy, not surgery plus adjuvant mFOLFIRINOX

THE QUOTED SURVIVAL BENEFIT IS A SECONDARY ENDPOINT IN A TRIAL WHOSE TWO PRIMARY ENDPOINTS BOTH FAILED. Recruitment missed its target and resection rate was not improved (and numerically favoured immediate surgery, 68% vs 55%). The trial was explicitly powered only to compare pooled resection rates at one-sided alpha 0.2, with 'no clinical criteria set to establish the overall success of the study'. A pathway that cites ESPAC5's HR 0.29 as evidence for neoadjuvant therapy is citing an underpowered secondary endpoint from a feasibility trial

NON-RECEIPT OF ALLOCATED TREATMENT: 5/55 (9%) allocated to neoadjuvant therapy never started it (2 gemcitabine/capecitabine, 1 FOLFIRINOX, 2 chemoradiotherapy - one death, one low platelets, one high bilirubin, two progressions); 3/31 (10%) allocated to immediate surgery never had surgery because of progression; and 4 patients were excluded from the analysis set after randomisation (1 consent withdrawal, 3 ineligible on histology or staging, including an autoimmune pancreatitis and a neuroendocrine tumour). Overall 17/90 (19%) did not follow their allocation or were removed

A 12-MONTH CAPPED FOLLOW-UP WITH 31 DEATHS PRODUCES AN IMPLAUSIBLY LARGE EFFECT. An HR of 0.29 from 19 deaths in a 31-patient control arm against 12 deaths across 55 neoadjuvant patients is the kind of estimate that regresses heavily toward the null with longer follow-up. Censoring everyone at one year also removes exactly the period in which early neoadjuvant deaths from toxicity would accumulate and in which immediate-surgery patients who survived the first year would catch up

TIME-ZERO AND IMMORTAL-TIME ASYMMETRY: neoadjuvant patients had a median 116-136 days between baseline CT and surgery versus 42 days for immediate surgery. Survival is measured from randomisation, which is correct, but the neoadjuvant arms had to survive and remain fit for 2-3 months to reach surgery - and the 7 who progressed on treatment and the 2 who died are a small number in a small trial, so chance determines how much of the survival difference is biological

THE FOUR ARMS ARE NOT BALANCED AT BASELINE in ways that favour the neoadjuvant groups: median CA19-9 was 802 kU/L in the immediate surgery arm versus 322-623 in the neoadjuvant arms, and 61% of the surgery arm were female versus 50-56% elsewhere. With 16-31 patients per arm, minimisation cannot be relied on, and a nearly three-fold higher CA19-9 in the control arm is a strong independent prognostic disadvantage that is not adjusted for

The chemoradiotherapy arm had the BEST pathological outcomes (37% R0, 25% node positive) but the WORST neoadjuvant survival (60% at 1 year), which directly contradicts the mechanistic premise that improved local clearance drives survival - and the authors themselves note the survival benefit was 'unrelated to the resection rate'

No multiplicity adjustment across four arms and a large secondary endpoint set; the abstract and results text give different p values for 1-year disease-free survival (0.016 vs 0.043), an internal inconsistency that should give pause when quoting the figure

The trial cannot answer which neoadjuvant regimen is better: FOLFIRINOX (84%) and gemcitabine plus capecitabine (78%) 1-year survival differ by less than the width of either confidence interval, both of which reach 100%

36521500.bottom_line: ESPAC5 is a feasibility trial that missed its recruitment target and found NO improvement in resection rate or R0 rate with short-course neoadjuvant therapy, but reported a striking 1-year survival advantage (76% vs 39%) as a secondary endpoint against a gemcitabine-era adjuvant comparator; it supports taking neoadjuvant chemotherapy seriously in borderline resectable disease and suggests chemotherapy beats chemoradiotherapy, but 90 patients and 12 months of follow-up cannot support the magnitude of effect it reports.

A pooled analysis across phase 1 dose exploration, phase 1 expansion and phase 2 mixes dose levels and eligibility thresholds (ECOG 2 allowed in phase 1, 0-1 in phase 2); the response rate is a weighted average over non-equivalent cohorts and is not reported by cohort or dose in the main text

Median OS of 6.9 months in a third-line-or-later population is indistinguishable from the natural history of that population; the paper does not claim otherwise, but a pathway citing 'activity in KRAS G12C pancreatic cancer' is reading a survival claim into an ORR

limitations: No limitations section. critique: Literature was 'selected by the authors' with no search strategy, no date limits, no screening flow and no second reviewer; a guideline that grades individual recommendations by level of evidence rests on an ungraded, unauditable evidence-identification step
Statements the panel considered 'justified standard clinical practice' are published without any grading at all, so the reader cannot tell which recommendations carry no evidence behind them

The grade II, E recommendation against neoadjuvant therapy in resectable disease predates PREOPANC-2, NORPACT-1 and the 2025 meta-analyses in this depot; the guideline is the most authoritative statement here but it is a 2023 snapshot, and a pathway page citing it as current needs to say what has appeared since

The borderline resectable recommendation rests on a five-study meta-analysis (HR 0.61) and on PREOPANC-1's 113-patient borderline subgroup — a subgroup of a trial whose overall primary endpoint was negative. The guideline does not say that, and the asymmetry between the firm adjuvant grades [I, A] and the hedged 'seems promising' language for induction is not explained to the reader in those terms

The panel's own failure to reach consensus on second-line oxaliplatin is reported in the text but does not appear as a graded recommendation, so a reader scanning the recommendation boxes will not see that the panel was split

No external funding was received and production costs were met by ESMO, but the disclosure list for the 14 authors runs to dozens of institutional and personal relationships with the manufacturers of the drugs being recommended (Amgen, AstraZeneca, BMS, Celgene, Merck, MSD, Pfizer, Servier and others); the guideline does not state how conflicts were managed in voting or whether conflicted authors abstained on specific recommendations

Much of the substance — incidence, risk-factor relative risks, adjuvant trial tables, resectable- and advanced-disease detail, the levels-of-evidence key, the MCBS and ESCAT tables — sits in supplementary material not present in this extraction, so the recommendation set can be verified here but the evidence tables behind it cannot
Medical writing and editing were provided by a commercial agency (Kstorfin Medical Communications) funded by ESMO, which is disclosed but means the final wording was not written solely by the panel
37678671.bottom_line: The authoritative European statement as of September 2023, and the single most important document in this depot for a pathway because it recommends against neoadjuvant therapy in resectable disease at grade II, E while supporting induction therapy for borderline resectable disease on weaker evidence — but it has no described literature search, substantial undisclosed-in-text conflicts across its panel, and predates the 2025 trials and meta-analyses.

limitations: Open-label design, with associated potential for outcome bias
The requirement for measurable disease and ECOG performance status 0 or 1 at screening
The absence of somatic or germline profiling information, so it is unknown whether BRCA-mutated patients benefited from platinum exposure in the NALIRIFOX group
Direct comparisons with PRODIGE 4 are not possible; that trial was limited to patients 75 or younger and conducted exclusively in France, whereas NAPOLI 3 was global with no age restriction
Cost implications and patient-reported quality-of-life outcomes were not reported and were still being analysed
critique: COMPARATOR: nab-paclitaxel plus gemcitabine - an active, contemporary standard. This is the appropriate comparator and the trial's main strength. But the regimen NALIRIFOX most needed to beat is FOLFIRINOX, and that comparison was NOT made. NALIRIFOX is FOLFIRINOX with liposomal irinotecan substituted and lower oxaliplatin, so the trial establishes a proprietary variant against a doublet while leaving unanswered whether it adds anything over generic FOLFIRINOX, whose own median in PRODIGE 4 was also 11.1 months

THE PRIMARY RESULT IS BARELY POSITIVE: HR 0.83 with a 95% CI upper bound of 0.99 and p=0.036 against a prespecified final-analysis alpha of 0.048 requiring HR below 0.844. The point estimate sits just inside the boundary the design set. A 1.9-month median gain at that level of statistical fragility is a weak basis for the paper's claim of a 'new possible reference regimen'

THE HIERARCHICAL TESTING SEQUENCE BROKE AT STEP THREE. Overall response rate (41.8% vs 36.2%, p=0.11) was not significant, so the formal evidence chain stops after progression-free survival; the duration-of-response and sensitivity-analysis p values are explicitly nominal
NON-RECEIPT OF ALLOCATED TREATMENT: 13/383 (3%) and 8/387 (2%) never received study treatment - low and balanced, a genuine strength

THE TRIAL RAN THROUGH THE COVID-19 PANDEMIC (February 2020 to August 2021) across 18 countries, with no analysis of pandemic-era disruption to treatment delivery, imaging or mortality; the open-label design and investigator-assessed progression make this more consequential than it would be for a blinded endpoint

PROGRESSION WAS ASSESSED BY INVESTIGATOR REVIEW ONLY, with no blinded independent central review, in an open-label trial - the setting APACT showed can shift a pancreatic recurrence endpoint by five months. The progression-free survival result (HR 0.69, p<0.0001), which is stronger than the survival result, is the endpoint most exposed to this

A LARGER SHARE OF NALIRIFOX PATIENTS WERE STILL ON TREATMENT AND STILL ALIVE AT DATA CUTOFF (12% vs 2% on treatment; 124 vs 102 censored), with only 16.1 months median follow-up. Immature follow-up with asymmetric censoring in the arm that wins is exactly the configuration in which an early positive signal attenuates, as it did between the 3-year and 5-year PRODIGE-24 reports

THE SENSITIVITY ANALYSIS CENSORING AT SUBSEQUENT THERAPY PRODUCES A 5.9-MONTH DIFFERENCE (15.1 vs 9.2 months) - three times the primary result. This is informative censoring: patients are removed from follow-up at a time determined by their own progression and their physician's decision, which differed systematically between arms (gemcitabine-based salvage after NALIRIFOX versus fluorouracil-based after the doublet). The figure should not be read as the 'true' effect

THE CROSS-TRIAL COMPARISON WITH PRODIGE 4 IS DONE IN THE DISCUSSION DESPITE THE AUTHORS' OWN DISCLAIMER, including a direct juxtaposition of NALIRIFOX's 3.5% neuropathy and 23.8% neutropenia against FOLFIRINOX's 9.0% and 45.7%. Those figures come from a French, age-capped, 342-patient trial run 15 years earlier with different growth-factor practice. The lower toxicity may simply reflect the lower oxaliplatin dose, which could equally be applied to generic FOLFIRINOX

QUALITY OF LIFE AND COST WERE NOT REPORTED, in a trial whose central practical question is whether a proprietary liposomal formulation justifies its price over generic irinotecan. Both arms had 86-87% grade 3+ adverse events, so the choice between them turns on tolerability profile and cost - exactly the two things not presented

THE FUNDER PARTICIPATED IN EVERY STAGE. Ipsen, which manufactures liposomal irinotecan (Onivyde), 'participated in study design, data collection, data analysis, data interpretation, and review and approval of the manuscript', and three authors are Ipsen employees, two of whom accessed and verified the underlying data. Nearly every academic author reports consulting or institutional funding from Ipsen among many other companies. The choice to test against nab-paclitaxel/gemcitabine rather than FOLFIRINOX is the comparator decision that most benefits the sponsor
37708904.n: 770 patients (383 NALIRIFOX, 387 nab-paclitaxel plus gemcitabine); safety population 749; 544 deaths at median follow-up 16.1 months
37708904.bottom_line: NAPOLI 3 is the first head-to-head phase 3 comparison of two active regimens in metastatic pancreatic cancer and shows NALIRIFOX modestly beats nab-paclitaxel plus gemcitabine (11.1 vs 9.2 months, HR 0.83, p=0.036) with equal overall grade 3+ toxicity and less neuropathy; the margin is narrow, the response-rate endpoint failed, follow-up is immature with asymmetric censoring, and the trial never compared the proprietary regimen with generic FOLFIRINOX, whose median survival in PRODIGE 4 was also 11.1 months.

limitations: Phase 2 design, so the results cannot be viewed as conclusive
Implementation of neoadjuvant FOLFIRINOX was challenging, and the use of full-dose rather than modified FOLFIRINOX may have increased toxicity and reduced compliance
Histological proof of PDAC was not mandatory before randomisation, so 11 patients (8%) with non-PDAC and generally better-prognosis diagnoses are included in the ITT analysis
Caution is needed with the hazard ratios, which are average hazard ratios over follow-up and should not be interpreted causally because baseline covariate balance can change over study time
The survival in the upfront surgery arm was markedly better than in previous reports, aligning with adjuvant rather than neoadjuvant trial populations
Only 60% of patients initiating neoadjuvant FOLFIRINOX completed all four cycles
No central radiology review was performed
critique: COMPARATOR: upfront surgery followed by adjuvant chemotherapy chosen at the treating oncologist's discretion. Adjuvant therapy was gemcitabine plus capecitabine (or gemcitabine monotherapy) until an August 2018 amendment permitted modified FOLFIRINOX. CONTROL ARM EXPOSURE TO MODERN ADJUVANT THERAPY WAS PARTIAL: only 19/44 (43%) of resected PDAC patients in the upfront arm actually received adjuvant mFOLFIRINOX, and 25/44 received a gemcitabine-based regimen. In the neoadjuvant arm only 13/51 (25%) received adjuvant mFOLFIRINOX. So the trial is not a clean test of neoadjuvant FOLFIRINOX against upfront surgery plus adjuvant mFOLFIRINOX

NON-RECEIPT OF ALLOCATED TREATMENT IS THE CENTRAL FLAW: 16/77 (21%) allocated to neoadjuvant FOLFIRINOX never received it - and crucially ALL 16 went straight to resection. Reasons were non-diagnostic repeat EUS sampling (6), persistent jaundice after stenting (2), another diagnosis (2), biliary infection (2), kidney failure (1), plus 3 who received a different neoadjuvant regimen. These 16 untreated-but-resected patients are counted in the neoadjuvant arm's ITT survival, which by itself means the ITT comparison is not a comparison of two delivered strategies. Only 1/63 (2%) in the upfront arm failed to undergo surgery

DILUTION COMPOUNDS NON-RECEIPT: of the 61 who did start FOLFIRINOX, only 37 (61%) finished four cycles and 16 (26%) received one or two cycles. Fewer than half the patients randomised to neoadjuvant therapy received the intended four-cycle course, so the trial tests an incompletely delivered strategy; PREOPANC-2 explicitly attributes NORPACT-1's null result partly to this (46% four-cycle completion vs 81% in PREOPANC-2)

THE PRIMARY ENDPOINT IS STATISTICALLY SIGNIFICANT IN FAVOUR OF UPFRONT SURGERY ONLY BY ITT AND ONLY AT A NON-STANDARD ALPHA. The trial was designed with a two-sided alpha of 0.15 as an exploratory study, so a p=0.032 difference in proportions and an HR whose lower bound touches 1.00 should not be read as evidence of HARM from neoadjuvant therapy; in the per-protocol analysis both comparisons are non-significant (p=0.14 and p=0.058). A pathway should not cite NORPACT-1 as showing neoadjuvant therapy is worse, only as failing to show it is better

ASYMMETRIC PRE-TREATMENT WORKUP: EUS-guided sampling and biliary stenting were performed only in the neoadjuvant arm (stenting 57% vs 16%). The upfront arm's path to the operating room was deliberately shorter and free of the stenting, cholangitis and post-ERCP pancreatitis complications that in fact derailed several neoadjuvant patients. The authors defend this as reflecting Nordic practice, but it is an asymmetry in risk exposure that is not part of the chemotherapy question

THE UPFRONT SURGERY ARM'S 38.5-MONTH MEDIAN IS AN OUTLIER. It far exceeds any comparable upfront-surgery arm (14.3 months in PREOPANC, 16.7 months in NEONAX) and resembles adjuvant-trial populations. Either the arm was favourably selected by chance in a 63-patient group, or the resectable, pancreatic-head-only, WHO 0-1, strongly favourable-biology eligibility produced a population with unusually good prognosis. With 63 patients and only 28 deaths, chance imbalance cannot be excluded, and the headline comparison is driven as much by an unusually good control arm as by a poor experimental one

SAMPLE SIZE AND POWER WERE REVISED MID-TRIAL (126 to 140 patients) and the primary endpoint itself was changed from a resected-patient analysis to an ITT analysis in 2018 after patients had been enrolled - decisions made with knowledge of accrual and diagnosis mix

ELEVEN NON-PDAC PATIENTS (8%) WITH BETTER-PROGNOSIS DISEASE REMAIN IN THE ITT DENOMINATOR, including 3 cholangiocarcinomas and 2 pNETs in the upfront surgery arm - enrichment of the control arm with favourable histology that the authors acknowledge but do not quantify in the survival analysis

Only 55% of patients randomised were followed long enough for events (77/140 deaths at median 22.7 months follow-up), so the median survival estimates, particularly the not-reached upper bound in the control arm, are unstable
The trial used full-dose, not modified, FOLFIRINOX without protocol-mandated G-CSF, which the authors concede may have driven the 58% grade 3+ toxicity rate and the compliance failure
38237621.n: 140 patients (77 neoadjuvant FOLFIRINOX, 63 upfront surgery); 119 resections; per-protocol population 115
38237621.bottom_line: NORPACT-1 failed to show any survival benefit from four cycles of neoadjuvant FOLFIRINOX in resectable pancreatic head cancer and its ITT primary endpoint favoured upfront surgery (18-month survival 60% vs 73%), but a fifth of the neoadjuvant arm never received the drug and went straight to resection, only 61% of those treated completed four cycles, and the control arm's 38.5-month median is far better than any comparable upfront-surgery cohort - so this is a failed-delivery trial, not evidence that neoadjuvant chemotherapy is harmful.

limitations: All included studies were retrospective; propensity matching in five can reduce but not eliminate bias, and matched on tumour characteristics but NOT consistently on chemotherapy regimen, with few studies accounting for first-line chemotherapy and even fewer reporting chemotherapy response or duration
Some key data were lacking and many data points were estimated by mathematical methods (the Parmar method applied to Kaplan-Meier curves)
Most included studies did not distinguish between types of chemotherapy
The power of the meta-regression may have been limited by missing data such as grading and CA 19-9 levels
Some studies were based on NCDB or SEER, which may have caused overlapping patient populations and data duplication

The non-surgical group was heterogeneous, including supportive care, palliative chemotherapy and multi-agent chemotherapy, with most receiving gemcitabine alone; most included studies also contained patients who did not receive 'curative' chemotherapy in the non-surgical group and the data could not be extracted
The authors state plainly that the adjusted HR 'remains an estimate based on mathematical calculations rather than direct evidence from real data', limiting definitive conclusions
critique: COMPARATOR: THE CONTROL ARM DID NOT RECEIVE MODERN SYSTEMIC THERAPY, AND THE PAPER PROVES IT. Roughly half of non-surgical patients received gemcitabine monotherapy, versus multi-agent regimens in the surgical arm, and the control group also contained best-supportive-care and palliative-bypass patients. The unadjusted HR of 0.41 is substantially a comparison of modern chemotherapy plus surgery against gemcitabine or no treatment - which is the single most important thing a pathway citing this paper needs to know, and it is confined to the discussion

THE ADJUSTED ANALYSIS IS THE HONEST RESULT AND IT IS CONDITIONAL AND MODEL-BASED. HR 0.18 for the pre-plus-post-chemotherapy scenario comes from fitting a multivariable meta-regression to SEVEN comparisons and then extrapolating to covariate values not observed in the data. With 7 data points and 11 candidate covariates, the model is grossly overfitted; the authors' own caveat that this is mathematics rather than evidence should be read as the conclusion, not a footnote

SIX STUDIES, ALL RETROSPECTIVE, I2 OF 64.5% - AND HETEROGENEITY IN THE PROPORTION ESTIMATES REACHES 96-98%. A pooled HR from this evidence base has a prediction interval far wider than the reported confidence interval, which is never presented

NONE OF THE INCLUDED STUDIES APPLIED A LANDMARK ANALYSIS, so immortal time bias is inherited wholesale. Kaslow et al. showed that a 12-month landmark alone raises median survival in a liver-only metastatic cohort from 9 to 26 months without surgery. The meta-regression corrects for chemotherapy exposure but nothing in it corrects for the requirement to survive to the operating theatre

THREE STUDIES WERE EXCLUDED FOR BEING 'very low quality and very disproportionate' AFTER their data were found partially extractable - a post-hoc exclusion on grounds that overlap with the direction of effect, and 315 records were excluded for language alone

OVERLAPPING POPULATIONS ARE ACKNOWLEDGED BUT NOT HANDLED. Pausch (SEER, n=518) and the Yun NCDB dataset (n=378) together supply two thirds of the patients and both draw on US national registries covering overlapping years (2010-2016), so the same patients may be counted twice and the two largest 'studies' are registry analyses with no resectability data at all

THE SURGICAL ARM'S DISEASE WAS GENUINELY LESS ADVANCED: 91% versus 85% oligometastatic, and 99% of liver resections were wedge excisions, meaning the operated metastases were small and peripheral. Balancing on the PROPORTION oligometastatic cannot balance the burden within that category

OPERATIVE MORBIDITY OF 53% IS REPORTED AS ACCEPTABLE because major morbidity was only 4%, but a 53% overall complication rate and 2% 30-day mortality in patients whose alternative is chemotherapy is a real cost that the abstract omits entirely

THE DEFINITION OF OLIGOMETASTASIS DIFFERED ACROSS EVERY STUDY (not reported, Hellman's qualitative definition, 3 or fewer, 4 or fewer with minor resection), and in the two largest registry studies it was ASSUMED rather than measured - the authors note Pausch's oligometastatic status was inferred 'on the basis of single-center retrospective studies' because SEER does not record metastasis number

The paper's conclusion that surgery 'could play a role, but only in highly selected cases' receiving both pre- and post-operative multi-agent chemotherapy is defensible, but it is indistinguishable from the proposition that patients who tolerate four to six months of multi-agent chemotherapy and remain fit for major surgery have favourable biology - which requires no surgical effect at all
39837137.n: 6 studies (7 comparisons; Yun et al. contributed two databases), 1348 patients: 667 (49.5%) surgical therapy, 681 (50.5%) non-surgical therapy
39837137.bottom_line: This meta-analysis of six retrospective studies finds an apparent halving of mortality with pancreatic plus liver resection in oligometastatic PDAC (HR 0.41), then shows through meta-regression that 87% of the heterogeneity is explained by how much chemotherapy each arm received - the control arms mostly got gemcitabine alone - and that a benefit survives adjustment only when patients receive both pre- and post-operative multi-agent chemotherapy (HR 0.18), an estimate the authors themselves call mathematical rather than empirical, and which no included study corrected for immortal time bias.

The study population was predominantly White (54%) and Asian (33%), with Black participants (3%) under-represented
NRG1 rearrangements are often missed by DNA-based sequencing because NRG1's large introns are not covered by standard panels; RNA-based sequencing, used predominantly here, is needed to find them

critique: There is no stated limitations paragraph as such; the caveats above are scattered through the discussion, and the single-group design is never named as a limitation even though every efficacy claim is uncontrolled

The primary endpoint is investigator-assessed response in an open-label trial, with blinded central review relegated to a secondary endpoint — the weaker assessment carries the primary claim, and the two differ by tumour type

The primary efficacy population is a post-enrolment construct: it requires a functionally predicted fusion, at least 24 weeks of follow-up before data cutoff, absence of other oncogenic alterations and no prior anti-HER3 exposure. 204 treated patients become 158 evaluable, and patients excluded for short follow-up are disproportionately early progressors

The pancreatic result is a prespecified subgroup of 36 patients within a basket trial whose sample size was justified only for the pooled estimate; the 95% CI of 25-59% is too wide to distinguish a major advance from a modest one

All 36 pancreatic patients were KRAS wild-type — a group that is perhaps 8-10% of PDAC and has a different natural history from KRAS-mutant disease. Since NRG1 fusions occur in well under 1% of PDAC, this is a very small slice of the disease and the paper gives no screening denominator
No progression-free or overall survival is reported for the pancreatic subgroup in the main text, only response and duration of response; a pathway cannot derive a survival claim from this paper
Nine fatal adverse events (4%) in 204 patients are reported as not treatment-related on investigator attribution alone, in an unblinded trial

Merus designed the trial, sponsor-employed statisticians analysed the data, and the sponsor together with the first and last authors drafted the manuscript with sponsor-funded medical writing across multiple drafts
39908431.n: 204 patients treated at 750 mg every 2 weeks; 158 in the primary efficacy population with measurable disease; 36 with pancreatic cancer
39908431.bottom_line: Validates NRG1 fusions as a drug target, with a 42% investigator-assessed response rate in 36 KRAS wild-type pancreatic patients, but provides no survival data for that subgroup, no control arm and no screening denominator, so it supports RNA-based fusion testing in KRAS wild-type PDAC rather than a quantified survival benefit.
39908431.funding: Merus (eNRGy, NCT02912949); sponsor-employed statisticians performed the analyses and sponsor-funded medical writing assistance was provided

limitations: The meta-analysis included some data from patients who had only a pancreatectomy or who had peritoneal rather than hepatic metastasis; excluding these studies would have left insufficient data to perform a meta-analysis at all

The retrospective nature of included studies introduces potential biases; surgeon discretion and institutional expertise are significant confounders that are difficult to measure, and high-volume hospitals with experienced surgeons are more likely to undertake complex resections
Heterogeneity in study design, control groups, resection cohorts and clinicopathological characteristics limits the conclusions from statistical analysis
No subgroup analysis by type of index operation, so no conclusions about pancreatoduodenectomy versus distal pancreatectomy; one study found a benefit for head resections and another the opposite
The lack of a consistent definition of hepatic oligometastasis complicates comparisons and underscores the need for a standardised classification
Heterogeneity in which RECIST classifications individual surgeons considered appropriate for surgery, and a wide array of cut-offs for biomarker response
No consensus on performance status cut-offs; most studies required 'good performance status' without quantification
critique: COMPARATOR: 'chemotherapy/palliation alone' pooled across seven studies, with no characterisation of what chemotherapy the control arms received. Unlike D'Ambra, this review performs NO meta-regression on chemotherapy exposure, so the single factor that D'Ambra showed explains 87% of the heterogeneity in essentially the same literature is left entirely unexamined - and the two reviews arrive at the identical HR of 0.41

I2 OF 12% IS REPORTED AS 'relatively low' HETEROGENEITY FROM SEVEN RETROSPECTIVE STUDIES WITH DIFFERENT DEFINITIONS OF OLIGOMETASTASIS, DIFFERENT CONTROL GROUPS AND DIFFERENT ERAS. D'Ambra's overlapping analysis found I2 64.5%. A near-zero I2 in this setting is more likely to reflect the small number of studies and the use of univariate HRs than genuine consistency, and the authors draw confidence from it

ONLY UNIVARIATE HAZARD RATIOS WERE POOLED, by explicit design, 'due to the degree of heterogeneity in multivariate analyses'. Pooling deliberately UNADJUSTED estimates from non-randomised studies, in a question dominated by selection, maximises confounding and the paper does not flag this as a limitation

IMMORTAL TIME BIAS IS NEVER MENTIONED. None of the included studies applied a landmark analysis, every surgical patient had to survive induction chemotherapy and remain fit, and Kaslow's demonstration that a 12-month landmark alone produces 26-month survival without surgery is absent from the discussion - a notable omission in a 2025 review of exactly this question

THE REVIEW'S OWN DATA UNDERCUT ITS CONCLUSION, AND IT DOES NOT SAY SO. A 32.5-versus-9.2-month gap generated by RECIST response criteria, best outcomes in patients with COMPLETE radiologic regression who had no metastasectomy at all, and three studies showing resected stage IV patients do worse than resected stage I-III patients, together describe a selection phenomenon. The conclusion instead reports 'a strong survival benefit in appropriately selected patients'

NOT PROSPECTIVELY REGISTERED (stated explicitly), and 71 of 142 screened records - half the evidence base - were added by 'citation searching and hand selection' rather than the database search, which is not a reproducible search strategy

THE POOLED COHORT IS NOT WHAT THE TITLE DESCRIBES: Hank contributes 26/93 patients with peritoneal or nodal rather than hepatic metastases, Crippa contributes 8/11 patients whose liver metastases had disappeared, Takeda 5/10 whose lesions were undetectable intraoperatively. The authors state that excluding these would leave too few studies to pool - which is an argument for not pooling

SUBSTANTIAL OVERLAP WITH D'AMBRA 2025 (Shao, Shi, Pausch, Hank and others appear in both) means the two apparently independent 2025 meta-analyses reporting HR 0.41 are largely the same patients, and a pathway that cites both is double-counting one evidence base

THE EXTEND TRIAL IS INVOKED AS RANDOMISED SUPPORT BUT TESTS SOMETHING ELSE: it is a phase 2 trial of metastasis-directed therapy (largely radiotherapy) added to systemic treatment, reporting progression-free survival, not pancreatectomy plus hepatectomy and not overall survival. Using it to reinforce a surgical conclusion is a category substitution

The review's genuinely useful output - that selection should rest on achievable R0 resection and demonstrated response rather than an arbitrary lesion count, and that CA19-9, margin, grade and preoperative chemotherapy predict outcome - is a narrative synthesis of heterogeneous reporting, not a quantitative finding, and the paper is clear that no meta-analysis of selection factors was possible
40002281.n: 16 studies in the review, 999 patients who underwent pancreatic resection for stage IV PDAC (637 synchronous resections, 48 metachronous, 259 from SEER with timing unknown); 7 studies pooled for the hazard ratio
40002281.bottom_line: This review of 16 studies and 999 resected patients pools a survival benefit for synchronous resection of liver-only metastatic PDAC (HR 0.41) and usefully catalogues how inconsistently patients are selected - but it pools only unadjusted hazard ratios, never addresses immortal time bias or the chemotherapy imbalance that a parallel 2025 meta-analysis showed explains most of the effect, and its own data (32.5 versus 9.2 months split by RECIST response, best outcomes in patients whose metastases had vanished) point to selection rather than surgery as the explanation.
40002281.funding: Funded internally by the University of Louisville Division of Surgical Oncology (no grant number). The authors declare no conflicts of interest.

limitations: Heterogeneity in the neoadjuvant and adjuvant regimens across trials, compounded by the evidence base changing over the period covered
Differing definitions and start times for progression-free survival across trials limit characterisation and need standardisation
Resectability definitions have changed over time and are not universally agreed; two trials (Golcher and Unno/Prep-02) had to be reclassified from resectable to borderline resectable
Prep-02/JSAP-05 was included from abstract form only and needs full publication to allow critical review
Ongoing trials (JASPAC, PANACHE01-PRODIGE48) could not be included because results were not published in a poolable form
Four of the nine trials closed early - two for poor accrual, one for outdated chemotherapy and one for superiority at interim analysis
critique: COMPARATORS ACROSS THE POOLED TRIALS ARE NOT INTERCHANGEABLE, AND ONLY ONE INCLUDED TRIAL GAVE THE CONTROL ARM MODERN ADJUVANT THERAPY. The paper's own Table 1 shows the upfront-surgery arms received adjuvant gemcitabine monotherapy (Casadei, Golcher, Jang), S-1 (Prep-02/JSAP-05), gemcitabine/nab-paclitaxel or PEXG (NEONAX, PACT-15), predominantly gemcitabine-based therapy in ESPAC5 (mFOLFIRINOX in only 2 of 43 patients) and mFOLFIRINOX in only NORPACT-1. Pooling these as one 'upfront surgery' comparator means the 0.73 HR is largely a comparison against obsolete adjuvant therapy, and the authors never say so

THE PAPER'S CONCLUSION OVERREACHES ITS OWN SUBGROUP TEST. It states neoadjuvant therapy 'should be regarded as standard of care' for borderline resectable disease on the basis of a subgroup HR of 0.60 whose between-subgroup interaction test was NOT significant (p=0.081) and whose own confidence interval nearly touches unity. The resectable-versus-borderline distinction is the single most consequential claim in the paper and it rests on an interaction that the data do not establish

THE OUTLIER REMOVAL IS POST HOC AND REMOVES THE ONE TRIAL WHOSE CONTROL ARM MOST RESEMBLES CURRENT PRACTICE. NORPACT-1 is excluded as an influence outlier precisely because it is the only trial giving upfront surgery plus adjuvant mFOLFIRINOX and the only one favouring upfront surgery. Dropping it tightens heterogeneity to zero by construction and manufactures a precise overall estimate; the honest reading is that the pooled estimate is unstable and depends on whether the modern comparator is included

DOUBLE-COUNTING AND UNIT-OF-ANALYSIS PROBLEMS: ESPAC5's four arms are entered in multiple ways (three separate neoadjuvant arms in some analyses, a pooled chemotherapy comparison in others), and PREOPANC is entered three times (overall, resectable, borderline). The tables show '9 trials' with '10' and sometimes '9 arms' in the same analysis, and a single upfront-surgery arm shared between several neoadjuvant comparisons inflates precision

SURVIVAL DATA FOR SEVERAL TRIALS WERE RECONSTRUCTED FROM KAPLAN-MEIER CURVES rather than taken from reported hazard ratios, which adds measurement error that the random-effects model treats as if it were sampling variation only

THE SERIOUS ADVERSE EVENT ESTIMATE IS INTERNALLY INCONSISTENT: RR 1.92 with a reported confidence interval of 1.28 to 1.89 does not contain its own point estimate (both in the abstract and in Table 4), so the harm estimate as published cannot be relied on even though its direction is clear and clinically important

FOLLOW-UP RANGES FROM 12 MONTHS (ESPAC5) TO 136 MONTHS, AND THE 12-MONTH TRIAL CARRIES THE MOST EXTREME EFFECT. Pooling hazard ratios across such disparate horizons assumes proportional hazards within and across trials, which PREOPANC's own data (1.4-month median difference with a 14% 5-year difference) directly contradicts

FOUR OF NINE TRIALS STOPPED EARLY, one of them for superiority at interim analysis (Jang), which systematically inflates the pooled effect; no small-study or early-stopping correction is applied beyond a funnel plot

The finding that adjuvant therapy rates did NOT differ (57.7% vs 55.6%) undercuts the principal mechanistic rationale for neoadjuvant sequencing, yet it is reported as a non-significant secondary outcome and not carried into the discussion of why the strategy might work

The authors include ESPAC5 and are the ESPAC5 investigators; no conflict is declared and none is financial, but the trial that contributes the largest single effect estimate was run by the review team
40126570.n: 9 trials, 1194 randomised patients (602 neoadjuvant, 592 upfront surgery); 517 resectable and 677 borderline resectable after NCCN reclassification
40126570.bottom_line: This meta-analysis of 1194 randomised patients supports neoadjuvant therapy in BORDERLINE resectable PDAC (HR 0.60) and not in resectable PDAC (HR 0.90), at the cost of a lower resection rate and twice the serious adverse events - but the subgroup difference is not statistically established, the pooled comparator is overwhelmingly obsolete adjuvant gemcitabine, and the headline estimate depends on post hoc removal of the only trial that used modern adjuvant chemotherapy in its control arm.
40126570.funding: The authors declare no funding and no conflict of interest.

limitations: The primary endpoint had to be CHANGED from overall survival to R0 resection rate because otherwise the study would not have been completed, which the authors acknowledge might have altered the type I error
The knowledge that R0 resection leads to better outcomes certainly changed the behaviour of the treating physicians
The radiotherapy protocol was described in detail but, for financial reasons, radiation was NOT centrally reviewed
Resectability was assessed locally and by a central tumour board, but it cannot be ruled out that uninvolved surgeons would have classified some cases as borderline resectable
Molecular parameters were not considered in the analysis
The study did not have sufficient statistical power to detect a difference in overall survival and can at best indicate which patients might benefit

Gemcitabine rather than capecitabine was given concurrently with radiotherapy; SCALOP data suggesting capecitabine-based chemoradiotherapy is better appeared after the trial had progressed too far to change the protocol
nab-paclitaxel plus gemcitabine was not opened as an additional arm when it became available in 2013-2014, to avoid further diversification
critique: COMPARATOR: continuation of the SAME induction chemotherapy. Because 84-87% of randomised patients had FOLFIRINOX induction, this is the only randomised trial to test consolidation chemoradiotherapy on a modern chemotherapy backbone - a genuine advance over LAP07. But no arm received upfront surgery or adjuvant therapy, so the trial speaks only to the radiotherapy question in unresectable disease

THE PRIMARY ENDPOINT WAS CHANGED MID-TRIAL FROM OVERALL SURVIVAL TO R0 RESECTION RATE, AND THE NEW ENDPOINT'S EFFECT SIZE WAS CALCULATED FROM UNBLINDED INTERIM DATA ON 180 ALREADY-ENROLLED PATIENTS, in which the R0 rate in one arm was already 'nearly twice as high' (30.2% vs 17.0%). The trial was then powered to detect exactly the difference its own interim data had shown. This is the most serious methodological problem in the depot: the sample size and the hypothesis were set using the result. The authors flag the type I error implication in one sentence but the trial still failed even this favourably chosen endpoint (P=.113)

THE HEADLINE POSITIVE RESULT IS CONDITIONAL ON SURGERY, WHICH WAS NOT RANDOMISED. R0 69% versus 50% is calculated among the 122 patients who went to the operating theatre - a group selected by panel recommendation, physician behaviour and patient fitness after treatment. The authors state plainly that physicians' knowledge of the R0 endpoint changed their behaviour, which is precisely the mechanism that could produce an R0 difference in the operated subset with no difference in the randomised population

NON-RECEIPT AND ATTRITION: 30/525 enrolled were excluded before induction (screening failure or withdrawal) and 159/495 (32.1%) progressed during induction and were never randomised. Within the randomised arms, 41/167 and 33/169 discontinued allocated treatment. The 336 randomised patients are the 64% of enrolled patients who survived and responded to three months of chemotherapy, and their 18-month median survival cannot be transferred to an unselected locally advanced population whose true median including non-randomised patients was 15 months

RADIOTHERAPY WAS NOT CENTRALLY REVIEWED, FOR STATED FINANCIAL REASONS, in a trial whose entire question is whether radiotherapy helps. LAP07, which did review radiotherapy, found 18% major deviations; CONKO-007 has no way to know its own delivery quality

THE 5-YEAR SURVIVAL CLAIM (10.1% vs 3.8%, and 24.8% vs 11.9% in operated patients) IS A TAIL COMPARISON INSIDE A NULL TRIAL, reported without a p value for the 5-year rates and with standard errors of 2.5% and 1.8% on a handful of patients (8 and 4 at risk at 60 months). The discussion asserts the 5-year rates were 'at least twice as high' with chemoradiotherapy; the trial's own survival analysis found HR 0.94, P=.57

GEMCITABINE WAS USED AS THE RADIOSENSITISER, which the authors concede SCALOP suggests is inferior to capecitabine, and gemcitabine induction patients (19% of the randomised population) had a far worse course - so the trial mixes two induction regimens with very different progression rates (47% vs 29%) and stratifies on but does not separately power for this

TOXICITY IS REPORTED ONLY AS A TABLE WHOSE NUMBERS ARE MISSING FROM THE EXTRACTED TEXT (the grade 3-4 adverse event counts in Table 3 did not extract), so the magnitude of the significant leukopenia and thrombocytopenia differences cannot be verified from this copy of the paper

AN 8% 30-DAY POSTOPERATIVE MORTALITY IN BOTH ARMS (5/60 and 5/62) IS HIGH and is presented as reassuring because it did not differ between arms. For a pathway weighing conversion surgery in locally advanced disease, one in twelve operative deaths is a material harm that the paper's conclusion ('without increasing postsurgical mortality') does not surface

THE CONCLUSION THAT 'SECONDARY SURGERY IS ASSOCIATED WITH A SUPERIOR PROGNOSIS' RESTS ENTIRELY ON A NON-RANDOMISED COMPARISON (HR 0.53) between patients fit and responsive enough to be operated and those who were not. This is the oldest confounding in surgical oncology and the paper does not adjust for response, CA 19-9 trajectory or performance status in that comparison

Industry disclosures are extensive for the first author (honoraria from MSD, AstraZeneca, Novocure, Merck Serono, Sennewald, Siemens Healthineers), relevant in a trial adjudicating radiotherapy, though funding came from German Cancer Aid
40802908.n: 525 enrolled, 495 received induction, 336 randomised (167 chemotherapy, 169 chemoradiotherapy); 122 underwent surgery; 450 deaths
40802908.bottom_line: CONKO-007 failed its primary endpoint - consolidation chemoradiotherapy after mostly FOLFIRINOX induction did not raise the overall R0 resection rate (25% vs 18%, P=.113) or survival (15 vs 14 months, HR 0.94) in unresectable pancreatic cancer - but it halved locoregional recurrence and, among the third of patients who reached surgery, raised R0 from 50% to 69%; its primary endpoint was changed mid-trial and powered from its own unblinded interim data, its surgical comparisons are not randomised, and its radiotherapy was never centrally reviewed.
40802908.funding: German Cancer Aid (Deutsche Krebshilfe 109284); the German Cancer Society is stated not to have influenced the design or analysis. Investigator-initiated. The first author reports honoraria from Merck Sharp & Dohme, AstraZeneca, Novocure, Merck Serono, Sennewald GmbH, MSD Oncology and Siemens Healthineers.

limitations: The cohort was heterogeneous, mixing resectable (65%) and borderline resectable (35%) disease, although Dutch criteria restricted borderline disease to limited vascular contact compared with NCCN definitions
No centralised review of radiology or pathology was performed, mitigated by nationally standardised radiology reporting and expert multidisciplinary review
Full-dose rather than modified FOLFIRINOX was scheduled, which may have increased toxicity relative to other recent trials
Data on subsequent anti-cancer treatment after recurrence were not collected
Quality of life, cost-effectiveness, biomarkers, recurrence patterns and surgical complications are reported separately, so this paper does not present the full secondary endpoint set
Only grade 3-5 adverse events were collected
The authors note the available evidence does not exclude a long-term survival benefit of neoadjuvant FOLFIRINOX
critique: COMPARATOR: this trial does NOT contain an upfront-surgery arm. Its comparator is the PREOPANC experimental regimen (neoadjuvant gemcitabine chemoradiotherapy plus adjuvant gemcitabine). The trial therefore cannot be cited for or against neoadjuvant therapy versus upfront surgery - only for the choice between two neoadjuvant regimens

NEITHER ARM RECEIVED MODERN ADJUVANT THERAPY. The FOLFIRINOX arm was scheduled for NO adjuvant treatment at all, and the comparator arm received adjuvant gemcitabine monotherapy, delivered in full to only 40% of randomised patients. A pathway that gives neoadjuvant chemotherapy and then adjuvant mFOLFIRINOX is not the strategy tested here, and the two arms are not matched on total intended systemic therapy (22 weeks vs 40 weeks of scheduled treatment)

NON-RECEIPT OF ALLOCATED TREATMENT: 10/185 (5%) in the FOLFIRINOX arm and 8/184 (4%) in the chemoradiotherapy arm never started allocated neoadjuvant therapy (early progression in 11 of these 18); 5 patients had surgery with no neoadjuvant study treatment; 2 chemoradiotherapy patients switched to FOLFIRINOX on local progression. Non-receipt was low and well balanced, which is a genuine strength relative to NORPACT-1

The analysis is MODIFIED intention-to-treat: 6 patients (3 per arm) were excluded after randomisation for retrospective ineligibility or immediate consent withdrawal. The exclusions are small and balanced, but this is not a pure ITT analysis

The design is a superiority trial that failed, not an equivalence or non-inferiority trial. The 95% CI for the HR extends to 1.13, so a 12% relative benefit for FOLFIRINOX is not excluded; the conclusion that 'both regimens may be considered' is a reasonable clinical reading but is NOT a demonstration of equivalence, and a pathway should not cite PREOPANC-2 as proof that the regimens are equal

Dose intensity in the FOLFIRINOX arm was substantially compromised (82% needed reductions, only 62% completed eight cycles, median relative dose intensity 0.81), so the trial tests a delivered regimen weaker than the protocol intended - a null result is partly a delivery result

The ypN0 and occult-metastasis differences run in opposite directions (nodal status favours chemoradiotherapy, avoidance of futile laparotomy favours FOLFIRINOX) and neither affected survival, reinforcing that nodal and margin status are poor surrogates in the neoadjuvant setting
Adjuvant gemcitabine in the comparator arm was given at the investigators' ability to deliver it rather than by protocol mandate, so the comparator arm is a mixture of strategies
No multiplicity adjustment was performed across the large secondary endpoint set, so the single significant nodal finding should be treated as exploratory
40945523.n: 369 patients in the modified ITT population (185 FOLFIRINOX, 184 chemoradiotherapy) of 375 randomised; 280 resections, 263 with PDAC confirmed
40945523.bottom_line: PREOPANC-2 shows that neoadjuvant full-dose FOLFIRINOX does not improve overall survival over neoadjuvant gemcitabine-based chemoradiotherapy (21.9 vs 21.3 months, HR 0.88, p=0.32), making gemcitabine chemoradiotherapy a defensible option when FOLFIRINOX is unsuitable; it says nothing about either regimen versus upfront surgery with modern adjuvant chemotherapy, and its wide confidence interval does not establish equivalence.
40945523.funding: Dutch Cancer Society and ZonMw (institutional, investigator-initiated); funders stated to have had no role in design, data collection, analysis, interpretation or writing. Several authors report institutional research funding or consulting from Servier, MSD, AstraZeneca, Medtronic, Intuitive Surgical, Roche, Oncosil, Galvani Bioelectronics, Nordic and others.

limitations: No limitations section is present in the extracted text; the methodology section describes the Oxford grading of evidence and the strong/weak recommendation scheme, which carries the implicit limitation that weakly graded recommendations rest on inconsistent evidence
critique: PRIMARY CRITIQUE: this file does not belong in a pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma depot. It is a liver transplantation candidate-evaluation guideline and cannot support any claim on a PDAC pathway page. Its presence should be treated as a depot curation error, and any pathway citation of it checked

The abstraction above is therefore structural only. The fields have been completed from the methodology and front matter rather than from disease-relevant content, because the spec requires one entry per file; nothing has been invented

Within its own domain, the guideline permits inclusion of articles not identified by the systematic search when the writing group thought them key, which reopens the selection to expert preference after a formal search was performed

Voting is recorded as agreement or disagreement per statement, but the extracted text does not report the vote counts or the threshold for adopting a statement, so the degree of panel consensus behind any individual recommendation is not visible
Conflict of interest is said to have been managed under the AASLD code, but the code's effect on specific recommendations (recusal, abstention) is not described
The guideline is funded by AASLD, a specialty society whose membership has an institutional interest in transplant volume; this is not a commercial conflict but is not discussed either
41405234.bottom_line: A liver transplantation candidate-evaluation guideline that has been misfiled into the PDAC depot; it establishes nothing about pancreatic cancer and should not be cited on a PDAC pathway.

limitations: As a phase 1-2 study the results should be interpreted with caution
Small subgroup sample sizes restrict the precision of antitumour-activity estimates and their interpretation by allele or co-mutation status
The single-group design precludes definitive comparison with standard treatment regimens
critique: The headline numbers most likely to be quoted (ORR 35%, PFS 8.5 months, OS 13.1 months) come from a subgroup of 26 patients defined by three simultaneous post hoc filters — RAS G12 allele, 300-mg dose, and exactly second line — selected from 168 treated patients after the data were seen; the confidence interval on response alone spans 17-56%

Response rates are reported as 'generally higher at 300 mg than at lower doses and in earlier rather than later lines', and 160-220 mg doses were pooled after the fact for 'substantial overlap in exposures'; dose groupings were therefore not fixed in advance

A reported 6-month overall survival of 100% (95% CI 100-100) in this subgroup is a sign of how selected it is: patients had to survive long enough on a tolerated dose at the right line to enter it, which is immortal-time selection rather than a treatment effect

Three exploratory 300-mg cohorts were removed from the report for 'differing end points or eligibility criteria', including the untreated-PDAC and RAS wild-type cohorts; the reader cannot see what those patients experienced

Grade 3 or higher adverse events of any cause occurred in 65% of patients and 48% of the 300-mg group needed dose modification, yet the discussion characterises the profile as 'mainly low-grade adverse events' on the strength of the treatment-attributed 30% figure, an attribution made by unblinded investigators

Revolution Medicines supported the study and provided medical writing through Nucleus Global; the paper's conclusion is framed as support for the sponsor's own phase 3 trial (RASolute 302), which is reported separately in this depot
Because no formal hypothesis was tested, there is no threshold the trial could have failed, and the safety primary endpoint has no prespecified acceptability bound either
42090791.n: 168 patients with RAS-mutated PDAC treated at 300 mg or less as second-line or later therapy (83 at 300 mg); RAS G12 second-line 300-mg subgroup n = 26 of 38 any-RAS
42090791.bottom_line: A dose-finding study whose stated primary purpose was safety, establishing that daraxonrasib is tolerable at 300 mg with 30% treatment-related grade 3+ toxicity and showing a 35% response rate in a 26-patient post hoc subgroup — hypothesis-generating support for the randomised trial, not evidence of benefit.
42090791.funding: Revolution Medicines; medical writing by Nucleus Global, an Inizio Company

limitations: The open-label design may have influenced adverse-event reporting, treatment modifications, and the decision not to begin treatment after randomisation; treatment was not initiated in 15.1% of the chemotherapy group, mostly by patient decision
Subgroup analyses were exploratory and limited by small sample sizes, particularly for uncommon RAS subtypes and patients with no identified RAS mutation
Given the rarity of those subgroups in PDAC, subgroup results should be interpreted descriptively
critique: COMPARATOR: investigator's choice from gemcitabine plus nab-paclitaxel, modified FOLFIRINOX, FOLFOX or liposomal irinotecan with fluorouracil, given per local prescribing practice. A median overall survival of 6.6 months in that arm is at the lower end of published second-line PDAC outcomes, and because regimen choice and dosing were unconstrained the control arm's quality is not auditable from this report

NON-RECEIPT OF ALLOCATED TREATMENT is the single most important asymmetry: 15.1% of the chemotherapy arm versus 2.8% of the daraxonrasib arm never started treatment, a five-fold difference. The authors attribute most of it to patient decision in an open-label trial, but patients who never start intravenous chemotherapy and are then counted in its intention-to-treat survival curve depress the comparator; no sensitivity analysis excluding or reweighting these patients is presented

Some chemotherapy-arm patients are stated to have become ineligible (ECOG above 1) between randomisation and treatment, which means the arms were not clinically equivalent at the moment treatment began — a problem an oral agent started the same day does not face

The primary population is the RAS G12 subpopulation, not all randomised patients; the all-comer result is a secondary endpoint and the non-G12 patients show HR 1.38 (0.60-3.17). A pathway should state that the benefit is established only for RAS G12 disease and that the non-G12 estimate points the other way

Blinded central review protects the progression-free survival endpoint, but overall survival in an open-label trial is still exposed to differential post-progression therapy, and the report does not detail subsequent treatments by arm

An HR of 0.40 for overall survival is extraordinarily large for second-line PDAC and should prompt the question of how much of it reflects a weakened comparator rather than drug effect; the toxicity data (grade 3+ 61.8% vs 69.6%, discontinuation 1.2% vs 11.2%) point the same way, in that the chemotherapy arm was both more toxic and far less adhered to

Revolution Medicines supported the trial, and the statistical analyses were performed and validated by the sponsor, with five author-employees of the sponsor; the sponsor also designed and funded the preceding phase 1-2 study
Quality-of-life and pain endpoints are time-to-deterioration measures in an unblinded trial, where knowledge of assignment affects both reporting and the timing of assessment
42223072.n: 500 randomised (248 daraxonrasib, 252 chemotherapy); more than 90% with RAS G12 mutations
42223072.bottom_line: The first randomised trial to show a survival gain from RAS inhibition in pancreatic cancer — median overall survival 13.2 vs 6.6 months, HR 0.40 in RAS G12 disease — but the size of the effect is inseparable from a control arm in which 15.1% never received their allocated chemotherapy and 11.2% stopped it for toxicity, and the non-G12 subgroup shows no benefit.
42223072.funding: Revolution Medicines; statistical analyses performed and validated by the sponsor
